2I.11 If any will forsake the LORD and their heart turns away from Him, then His anger shall be aroused against them, and many evils and troubles shall befall them.

precepts.text: After Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, a man of Issachar, who dwelt in Shamir in mount Ephraim and judged Israel twenty and three years. After him arose Jair, a Gileadite, who judged twenty and two years and had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, with thirty cities called Havoth-jair in Gilead, named for where he was from.
precepts.point: And concerning the judges, every one by name, whose heart went not a whoring nor departed from the Lord, let their memory be blessed. That sends us to the book of Judges to name them.

precepts.text: The Lord left nations to prove Israel, that the generations which had not known all the wars of Canaan might be taught war, and to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
precepts.point: Notice it says to defend Israel. Israel was in the land, but do not forget that the Lord had left nations among us, so the judges had to defend the people.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why:
Notice it says Tola arose “to defend Israel”. Israel was in the land, but do not forget that the Lord had left nations among us: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan”. He left them “to teach them war”, that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might learn it, and “to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.”

Those nations were the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that dwelt in mount Lebanon. With them left in the land, the judges had to defend the people; that is why Tola’s twenty and three years are described as defending Israel.

precepts.text: One of the curses for breaking the laws: thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and there shall be no might in thine hand.
precepts.point: Moreover the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, which shows those tribes dwelling in their own allotments on the other side; so that Israel was sore distressed.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why: “he sold them into the hands of the Philistines, and into the hands of the children of Ammon.” Israel was serving their gods, so the Lord sold Israel to them. This is one of the curses for breaking the laws: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.” Eighteen years the tribes on the other side Jordan, Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh in their allotments in Gilead, were vexed and oppressed: given unto another people, with no might in their hand.

precepts.text: Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity; the curse of the law was already working on Israel in the land.
precepts.point: Moreover the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, which shows those tribes dwelling in their own allotments on the other side; so that Israel was sore distressed.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why: “Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” The curse of the law was already working on Israel while they were still in the land. The Lord sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the children of Ammon; Ammon oppressed Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead eighteen years, then passed over Jordan against Judah, Benjamin and the house of Ephraim in their own allotments, “so that Israel was sore distressed.” Israel served the gods of those nations, and the Lord gave Israel’s sons and daughters to them.

precepts.text: The whole cycle of the book of Judges in one passage: Israel was disobedient, cast thy law behind their backs, and slew the prophets; the Lord delivered them into the hand of their enemies; in the time of their trouble they cried, and he heard from heaven and gave them saviours who saved them; and after they had rest, they did evil again before thee.
precepts.point: Yet ye have forsaken me, and served other gods: wherefore I will deliver you no more. Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation. The Lord is not unrighteous; he gave a fair covenant: do right and he is with you above all nations, do wrong and you go into captivity. He will not break his word, and everybody's grace is not the same.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why:
The whole cycle of the book of Judges in one passage. “Nevertheless they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee”. “Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them: and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” Those saviours are the judges. “But after they had rest, they did evil again before thee: therefore leftest thou them in the hand of their enemies”.

That is what the Lord rehearsed to Israel here: he delivered us from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the children of Ammon, the Philistines, the Zidonians, the Amalekites and the Maonites, over and over, all through the early chapters of this book; yet we forsook him and served other gods. Now that the enemy had destroyed on one side of Jordan and was crossing over against Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim, Israel wanted to confess.

The Lord is not unrighteous. He gave a fair covenant: do right and he is with you above all nations, do wrong and you go into captivity. He will not break his word, and everybody’s grace is not the same. So this time he said, “Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation.”

points: Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation. Let white Jesus deliver the Christians from Trump.
After Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, a man of Issachar; he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.
Notice it says to defend Israel. Israel was in the land, but do not forget that the Lord had left nations among us, so the judges had to defend the people.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: After him arose Jair, a Gileadite, and judged Israel twenty and two years. He had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities in the land of Gilead, which are called Havoth-jair unto this day; and Jair died and was buried in Camon.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD. That is the cycle of this whole book: after a judge died and Israel had peace and safety for a while, the people went right back into their sin, just like always.

Israel served Baalim and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, the gods of Zidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines, and forsook the LORD, and served not him. Ashtaroth is Ishtar or Astarte, the so called queen of heaven; the heathen carried the same goddess under different names, the same one the Greeks called Aphrodite.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the children of Ammon. Israel was serving their gods, so the Lord sold Israel to them.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: Eighteen years they vexed and oppressed all the children of Israel that were on the other side Jordan, in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead: that was Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh in their allotments across the river.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: Moreover the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, which shows those tribes dwelling in their own allotments on the other side; so that Israel was sore distressed.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Israel cried unto the LORD, saying, We have sinned against thee, both because we have forsaken our God, and also served Baalim. The enemy had destroyed on one side of Jordan and was crossing over against Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim, so now Israel wanted to confess.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The Lord answered by rehearsing the deliverances: did not I deliver you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines? the Zidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites did oppress you, and ye cried to me, and I delivered you out of their hand. All through the early chapters of this book he kept delivering us over and over.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: Yet ye have forsaken me, and served other gods: wherefore I will deliver you no more. Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation. The Lord is not unrighteous; he gave a fair covenant: do right and he is with you above all nations, do wrong and you go into captivity. He will not break his word, and everybody's grace is not the same.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Israel said unto the LORD, We have sinned: do thou unto us whatsoever seemeth good unto thee; deliver us only, we pray thee, this day. And they put away the strange gods from among them and served the LORD. This time the repentance came with action.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: And his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel. The Most High loves Israel; it grieved him to have his own children in captivity, but he cannot break his word, so the repentance had to come first. That is also why Christ was sent to die for our sins, so we could have a chance to return to him in the last days.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Ammon were gathered together and encamped in Gilead, and the children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpeh.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The people and princes of Gilead said one to another, What man is he that will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? he shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead. That question is answered in chapter 11.
